newsitem.title: JAPAN: Non-bank Koei Corp says to seek liquidation.
newsitem.headline: Non-bank Koei Corp says to seek liquidation.

text.p: Non-bank lender Koei Corp, of which the Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd (IBJ) is a major creditor, said on Thursday it would seek liquidation under court protection by the end of March.
"It is true that we will go in that direction (to seek liquidation). We will probably apply to the Tokyo District Court for special liquidation by the end of March," a Koei official said.
An IBJ spokesman said Koei had informed the bank of its liquidation plan and that the bank would agree to the plan.
Koei's debts totalled 259.4 billion yen at the end of March 1996, of which 61.2 billion was loans from IBJ, the Koei official said.
Koei's other creditors include Sumitomo Trust and Banking Co Ltd, which has outstanding loans of 9.6 billion yen to Koei, the Koei official said.
Koei will also seek approval for its liquidation plans from its other creditor banks, the official said.

The company, suffering from aggressive lending for real estate projects, decided to seek liquidation because it will have completed a five-year restructuring programme in February, the Koei official said.
"We will have completed selling the properties we planned to sell under the restructuring programme," the Koei official said.
The amounts earned from the sales will not be as large as originally expected due to the sluggish real estate market, he said.
